docs.title: HIVE
docs.text:
Hydrodynamic Identification and Validation Environment

HIVE is a Python framework for wave energy converter (WEC) hydrodynamic modelling, identification, and model benchmarking.

docs.title: What HIVE does
docs.text:
HIVE provides structured pipelines to:

  • Process CFD simulation data
  • Validate existing physics and data-based models against CFD reference data
  • Identify model parameters and data-driven surrogates from CFD reference data

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• BEM-based linear and weakly-nonlinear hydrodynamic model
  • Viscous drag identification
  • PI gain identification for PTO control
  • Multiple and various data-based model (wave-to-force-to-velocity state-space, system identification for nonlinear dynamic (SINDY), neural network)
  • model benchmarking through large metric bank

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• environment surrogate
  • A HydroSphere BEM pickle file (r5.pkl is the project default) placed under source/models/bem/ for validation and/or identification pipeline
  • A reference raw dataset folder for placed under 'data/cfd/' for handle pipeline
  • A reference handled dataset (.csv) for validation and identification pipeline placed under data/handled/
  • A model folder with model definition (.json) for validation and/or identification pipeline placed under source/models/

docs.title: Quick start example
docs.text: All scripts are run as modules from inside the code/ folder. A minimal test case is provided using r5.pkl as BEM model and out_Case_65_20_120000_-430000_example as raw reference dataset. When repeating the test run again, a user command is required, choose [1] erase and redo all. More information is available in the user manual.

docs.title: Process raw CFD data
docs.text:
Run it with: 

python -m script.run_handle_data --case example_cases.json

Outputs land in data/handled/example_cases/. When repeating the test run again, a user command is required, choose [1] erase and redo all. More information is available in the user manual.

docs.text:
Run it with: 

python -m script.run_identify --case example_identify.json

Outputs land in source/models/example_identify/ for identification results. When repeating the test run again, a user command is required, choose [1] erase and redo all. More information is available in the user manual.

docs.title: Metric
docs.text: Name Description Default direction "rmse_x" RMSE of displacement \(x\) minimize "rmse_xdot" RMSE of velocity \(\dot{x}\) minimize "nrmse_x" Normalised RMSE of \(x\) minimize "nrmse_xdot" Normalised RMSE of \(\dot{x}\) minimize "mean_P_abs" Mean absorbed power \(P_{abs}\) maximize "rmse_P_abs" RMSE of absorbed power minimize

docs.title: Model
docs.text: Time margins — t_warmup and t_causal are derived automatically from the BEM IRF data of each loaded model and are not JSON inputs. The most conservative values across all models are applied uniformly to clip every simulation before metric computation.

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text: HIVE is built around three pipelines ran via scripts, run_handle_data, run_validate and run_identify, each driven by a JSON input file and writing outputs to a structured folder.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Script What it does Config location Output location run_handle_data Reads raw CFD time series, applies cut times and optional resampling, computes wave parameters and hydrodynamic quantities, saves one processed dataset per case inputs/handle_case/<name>.json data/handled/<name>/ run_validate Loads processed datasets and a model.json, runs forward simulations via SimRun, computes metrics against the CFD reference, produces scatter plots over the \((H_s, T_e)\) parameter space inputs/validate_case/<name>.json out/validated_case/<name>/ run_identify Uses a scheme module (viscous_drag, pi_gain, or linear_si) to identify model parameters from CFD data, updates model.json with the result inputs/identify_case/<name>.json models/<name>/ + models/<name>/identification/

Each script read the input .json file --case <name>.json argument. The stem of that filename becomes the output folder name — choose stems that are short, lowercase, and use underscores (e.g. r5_reg).

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
The outputs are data (.csv), metrics (.json) and plots (.png and .pkl). Every plot is saved as both .png (for quick viewing) and .pkl (interactive Matplotlib figure). Reload a .pkl interactively with option [3] at the rerun prompt, or directly:

import pickle, matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig = pickle.load(open("plots/sea_state.pkl", "rb"))
plt.show()

docs.title: run_handle_data
docs.text: Processes raw CFD time series into a standardised format ready for validation and identification.

docs.title: first run
docs.text:
python -m script.run_handle_data --case <name>.json

Config files ´.json´ live in inputs/handle_case/. The filename stem becomes the output folder name under data/handled/.

docs.title: rerun options
docs.text:
When the output folder already exists, the script prompts:

[1] erase and redo all     — reprocess + replot from scratch
[2] stop, do nothing
[3] load saved figures     — reopen existing .pkl plots interactively
[4] remake figures only    — reuse processed CSVs, regenerate plots

Option [4] is useful when tuning plot parameters without reprocessing data.

docs.title: what it does
docs.text:
1. Reads each CFD case folder from data/cfd/
  2. Instantiates a DataHandle object per case
  3. Calls processData() — computes radiation force, hydrostatic force, linear excitation force (fe_lin), and absorbed power
  4. Optionally resamples to a target dt
  5. Saves processed data and wave parameters to data/handled/<name>/data/
  6. Generates and saves plots to data/handled/<name>/plots/

Field Type Required Description wave_type "irr" | "reg" yes Wave type used in the CFD simulation cut_time [float, float] yes Seconds to discard from [start, end] of the raw signal. Use 0 to keep to the edge duration float | null no Maximum duration (s) to retain after the start cut. null keeps all remaining data hydro_sphere_pkl string yes Stem of the BEM .pkl file in source/models/bem/. e.g. "r5" loads r5.pkl dt float | null no Target resampling timestep (s). null keeps the original CFD timestep cases list[dict] yes List of CFD cases to process (see cases) plot_options dict no Controls which plots are generated (see plot_options)

docs.title: cases
docs.text:
Each entry in cases:

Field Type Required Description T float yes Wave period from the CFD folder name (s) H float yes Wave height from the CFD folder name (m) damping int yes PTO damping coefficient (N·s/m) stiffness int yes PTO stiffness coefficient (N/m). Use negative for spring-like reactive control tag string | null no Optional suffix appended to the CFD folder name and output label plot bool no Whether to include this case in plots. Default: true

Each CFD case is assigned a label derived from the CDF folder case name which contain parameters. An optional "tag" field in the case config appends a suffix. The label is used as the CSV filename stem and as the series label in plots:

Hs{H}p{dec}_Te{T}p{dec}_d{damping}_k{stiffness}_{tag}

Example: Hs2p0_Te8p0_d120000_k-280000_example

docs.title: plot_options
docs.text: Field Type Description sea_state bool Wave spectrum, elevation time series, and sea state grid power bool Absorbed power time series, power grid, and accumulated energy dynamics bool Displacement, velocity time series, and phase plot (x vs ẋ) hydro bool Hydrodynamic force breakdown: draft, linear forces, CFD forces, linear vs nonlinear comparisons 3d bool 3D scatter of displacement, velocity, and wave elevation variable list of strings | false One time-series plot per named column from _data.csv. e.g. ["fe_lin", "x"]

docs.title: run_identify
docs.text: Identifies model parameters or data-driven surrogates from CFD reference data using a pluggable scheme system.

docs.title: first run
docs.text:
python -m script.run_identify --case <name>.json

Config files <name>.json live in inputs/identify_case/. The filename stem becomes the output folder name under source/models/.

docs.title: rerun options
docs.text:
When the output folder already exists, the script prompts:

[1] erase and redo
[2] stop, do nothing
[3] load saved figures     — reopen existing .pkl plots interactively
[4] save with date suffix  — run and save under <name>_YYYYMMDD (keeps existing folder)

Option [4] is useful to keep previous identification results while running a new one with same JSON input.

docs.title: available schemes
docs.text: Scheme Description Note "viscous_drag" identify a viscous drag coefficient given a base model to fit CFD reference data see Scheme: viscous_drag "pi_gain" find optimal PI gain (stiffness and damping coefficient) to maximize or minimize an objective, absorbed power for instance see Scheme: pi_gain

docs.title: what it does
docs.text:
Run an optimization depending on the chosen identification scheme and based on a chosen model. More explicitely:

  1. Loads the base model definition from source/models/<base_model>/model.json
  2. Creates a DDFeed — loads training data and runs scheme.prep()
  3. Creates an Optimizer — owns simulation helpers and delegates to scheme.run()
  4. Computes time margins (t_warmup, t_causal) from the base model and BEM data
  5. Saves identified parameters, result JSON, simulation CSVs and plots to source/models/<name>/identification/

docs.title: Scheme: viscous_drag
docs.text:
Identifies the quadratic drag coefficient \(c_v\) in \(f_{visc} = -c_v |\dot{x}| \dot{x}\) for:

  • per-case — \(c_v\) fitted independently to each wave case
  • global — single \(c_v\) fitted across all cases pooled together → corresponds to the model output written to model.json

docs.title: input JSON config
docs.text:
{
  "scheme": "viscous_drag",
  "waves_train": [
    "example_cases"
  ],
  "base_model": "linear_sphere_r5",
  "scheme_params": {
    "base_force": "fe_lin",
    "type": ["force", "response"],
    "search": ["opt", "grid"],
    "c_v_min": 0,
    "c_v_max": 150000,
    "n_points": 10,
    "objective": "rmse_x"
  },
  "solver": {
    "method": "RK4",
    "dt": 0.05,
    "interpolation": {
      "fe": true,
      "eta_hs": true
    }
  }
}

docs.title: top-level entries
docs.text: Field Type Options / values Multiple entry (list) Description waves_train string Handled data folder name under data/handled/ Yes. All entries are loaded and merged into a single flat pool of wave cases Identification data base_model string model folder name under source/models/.See Model No Physics-bases model to augment with viscous drag. scheme_params dict see scheme_params table below No Scheme-specific parameters solver dict see Solver No Simulation solver settings

docs.title: scheme_params
docs.text:
Field Type Default Options / values Multiple entry (list) Description type string — "force", "response" Yes Identification type. "force" fits \(c_v\) to match \(F_{hyd}\) ; "response" fits \(c_v\) to match \(x\), \(\dot{x}\) search string — "opt", "grid" Yes Search method. "opt" uses a bounded scalar optimiser ; "grid" sweeps a uniform grid over \([c_{v,min},\ c_{v,max}]\) base_force string "fhyd_lin" any column present in the DataHandle dataset No Force column (\(f_{col}\)) subtracted to reference force \(f_{hyd}\) type = "force", such as \(f_{hyd} = f_{col} + f_{visc}\) c_v_min float 0.0 any non-negative float [N·s²/m²] No Lower bound of the \(c_v\) search range c_v_max float 5000.0 any positive float [N·s²/m²] No Upper bound of the \(c_v\) search range n_points int 100 any positive integer No Grid resolution — used only when search = "grid" objective string "rmse_x" Any available metric. see Metric No Metric used to score \(c_v\) candidates

The four possible type × search method combinations are: force_opt, force_grid, response_opt, response_grid. Pass lists to run several at once.

docs.title: Scheme: pi_gain
docs.text: Identifies per-sea-state PI controller gains \((B_{pto},\ K_{pto})\) that maximise an objective (default: mean absorbed power).

docs.title: input JSON config
docs.text:
{
  "scheme": "pi_gain",
  "base_model": "linear_sphere_r5",
  "waves_train": [
    {"type": "cfd_case", "case_name": "example_cases"},
    {"type": "synthetic", "type_wave": "irr", "T": 7.0, "H": 2.0, "duration": 120.0, "gamma": 3.3}
  ],
  "scheme_params": {
    "method": ["analytical", "grid", "opt"],
    "B_min": 0,
    "B_max": 500000,
    "K_min": -200000,
    "K_max": 0,
    "n_B": 5,
    "n_K": 5,
    "B_init": 200000,
    "K_init": -100000,
    "objective": {"name": "mean_P_abs", "direction": "maximize"},
    "stability": {"enabled": true, "r": 5.0},
    "n_jobs": -1
  },
  "solver": {
    "method": "rk4",
    "dt": 0.05,
    "interpolation": {"fe": true, "eta_hs": true}
  }
}

docs.title: top-level entries
docs.text:
Identification runs on all of them together — there is no separate pass per entry.

Field Type Options / values Multiple entry (list) Description waves_train dict See waves_train Yes. All entries are loaded and merged into a single flat pool of wave cases Sea states profile, synthetic or CFD based, on which is based the PTO gain identification base_model string model folder name under source/models/. See Model No Model on which is based the PTO gain identification scheme_params dict see scheme_params below No Scheme-specific parameters solver dict see Solver No Simulation solver settings

docs.text: Field Type Default Options / values Description type string — "synthetic" for wave generated by addition of regular wave components. "cfd_case" for wave elevation from CFD based data Wave elevation source case_name string — handled data folder case name under data/handled/ handled data folder case name. Only when type = "cfd_case" wave_type string "reg" "reg" (regular sinusoid) · "irr" (irregular JONSWAP) Wave type. Only when type = "synthetic" T float — any positive float (s) Wave period (regular) or energy period (irregular). Only when type = "synthetic" H float — any positive float (m) Wave height (regular) or significant wave height (irregular). Only when type = "synthetic" gamma float None any positive float JONSWAP peak enhancement factorwave_type = "irr". Only Only when type = "synthetic" and wave_type = "irr" duration float 100.0 any positive float (s) Signal duration. Only when type = "synthetic"

docs.title: scheme_params fields
docs.text:
Field Type Default Options / values Multiple entry (list) Description method string "opt" "analytical" (from linear potential flow theory, does not consider bounds values)· "opt" using an optimizer· "grid" doing a grid-search· or a list of several Yes Identification method(s). Pass a list to run and compare multiple methods in one execution B_min float 0.0 any float [N·s/m] No Lower bound for \(B_{pto}\) search B_max float 1e6 any float [N·s/m] No Upper bound for \(B_{pto}\) search K_min float -1e6 any float [N/m] No Lower bound for \(K_{pto}\) search K_max float 1e6 any float [N/m] No Upper bound for \(K_{pto}\) search n_B int 20 any positive integer No Grid points along \(B\) axis — used only when method = "grid" n_K int 20 any positive integer No Grid points along \(K\) axis — used only when method = "grid" B_init float midpoint of [B_min, B_max] any float [N·s/m] No Initial value for the "opt" optimiser K_init float midpoint of [K_min, K_max] any float [N/m] No Initial value for the "opt" optimiser objective dict {"name": "mean_P_abs", "direction": "maximize"} see Metric for ´"name´, "maximize" or "minimize" for ´"direction"´ No Metric used to score \((B, K)\) candidates stability dict {"enabled": false, "r": 5.0} enabled: true / false · r: float (m) No Early-stop check: aborts integration if \(\|x - \eta\| > r\). r defaults to buoy radius if not set n_jobs int 1 any integer · -1 = all CPU cores No Parallel workers for "grid" search via joblib

The "analytical" method is based on linear potential flow theory and hence limited to regular waves. While it does not hold for irregular waves, the energy period is still used.

docs.title: run_validate
docs.text: Runs physics models against CFD reference data or synthetic wave signals and computes validation metrics across all (model, wave source, solver) combinations.

docs.title: first run
docs.text:
python -m script.run_validate --case <name>.json

Config files <name>.json live in inputs/validate_case/. The filename stem becomes the output folder name under outputs/validated_case/.

docs.title: rerun options
docs.text:
When the output folder already exists, the script prompts:

[1] erase and redo all
[2] stop, do nothing
[3] load saved figures     — reopen existing .pkl plots interactively
[4] remake plots only      — reuse existing CSVs, regenerate plots and metrics

Option [4] is useful after changing plot_options without rerunning all simulations.

docs.title: what it does
docs.text:
Runs all (model, wave source, solver) combinations and compares simulated outputs against CFD reference data. More explicitly:

  1. Loads all model definitions from source/models/<name>/model.json
  2. Resolves wave sources — loads CFD cases or generates synthetic waves
  3. Checks solver dt against CFD reference dt; prompts to continue if they differ
  4. Computes conservative time margins (t_warmup, t_causal) from BEM data across all models
  5. Runs simulations for all (model, wave, solver) combinations and clips to valid time window
  6. Saves time-series CSVs, computes metrics, and generates plots to outputs/validated_case/<name>/

docs.title: Input JSON config
docs.text:
{
  "models": [
    {"name": "linear_sphere_r5"},
    {"name": "example_identify"}
  ],
  "wave_sources": [
    {"type": "cfd_case", "case_name": "example_cases"},
    {
      "type": "synthetic",
      "wave_type": "irr",
      "T": 7.0,
      "H": 2.0,
      "gamma": 3.3,
      "duration": 120.0,
      "dt": 0.05,
      "pto": {"damping": 120000, "stiffness": -430000}
    }
  ],
  "solvers": [
    {"method": "RK4", "dt": 0.05, "interpolation": {"fe": true, "eta_hs": true}}
  ],
  "plot_options": {
    "states": true,

docs.title: Model types
docs.text:
A model in HIVE is a folder under models/ containing a model.json file. The JSON records the model's physics components, identified parameters, and metadata. Currently supported model types:

Model key Description linear Cummins equation with radiation state-space, linear PTO linear_viscous As linear, plus quadratic drag $c_v

Models identified by run_identify inherit a base model's model.json and add or update the identified parameters.

docs.title: model.json structure
docs.text:
{
  "type": "linear_viscous",
  "hydro_sphere_pkl": "r5",
  "radiation": {
    "A": [[...], ...],
    "B": [[...]],
    "C": [[...]],
    "D": [[...]]
  },
  "hydrostatic": {
    "K_hs": 142000.0
  },
  "added_mass_inf": 450.0,
  "mass": 1200.0,
  "c_v": 1850.0,
  "t_warmup": 15.0,
  "t_causal": 3.2
}

The radiation block holds the state-space matrices \((A_{rad}, B_{rad}, C_{rad}, D_{rad})\) fitted from the BEM IRF. These are written by run_handle_data during the first call that initialises the BEM data.

docs.title: SimRun
docs.text:
SimRun is the class responsible for running a single forward simulation. It:

  1. Loads the model definition from model.json
  2. Instantiates the radiation state integrator
  3. Steps the ODE forward using the chosen solver
  4. Returns a dataset attribute (a pandas.DataFrame) with the same column schema as DataHandle

Because SimRun and DataHandle expose the same .dataset and .label interface, they can be mixed in plotter calls.

docs.title: ODE solvers
docs.text:
The solver block in validate and identify configs selects the numerical integrator:

"solver": {
  "method": "RK4",
  "dt": 0.05,
  "interpolation": {}
}
Method Description RK4 4th-order Runge–Kutta (recommended) RK2 2nd-order Runge–Kutta (Heun's method) euler Forward Euler (1st order, fast but inaccurate)

The integration timestep dt is independent of the CFD data's native timestep. HIVE interpolates the forcing signals (wave elevation, excitation force) onto the solver grid using the scheme specified in interpolation.

docs.title: Warmup period
docs.text:
The radiation state-space system starts at rest (\(\mathbf{z}_{rad} = 0\)). It takes several wave periods for the radiation states to converge to their quasi-steady values. HIVE computes t_warmup automatically from the pole magnitudes of \(A_{rad}\):

\[ t_{warmup} = \frac{-\log(\epsilon)}{\min_k |\text{Re}(p_k)|} \]

where \(\epsilon\) is a small tolerance (default \(10^{-3}\)) and \(p_k\) are the eigenvalues of \(A_{rad}\). The value is logged in run.log and saved in result.json.

Metrics are computed only over \([t_{warmup},\; T_{end} - t_{causal}]\).

docs.title: Why interpolation is needed
docs.text:
The excitation force \(f_e^{lin}\) and wave elevation \(\eta\) are precomputed on a fixed grid — the timestep of the handled CFD data (set by dt in the handle config). The ODE solver may use a different timestep. At each stage of the integrator (e.g. the four stages of RK4), the forcing signals must be evaluated at intermediate time points that generally do not fall on the original grid, requiring interpolation.

Note that \(f_e^{lin}\) is state-independent — it does not depend on \(x\) or \(\dot{x}\) — so it is fully precomputed before integration begins. This is unlike the radiation force \(f_{rad}\), which is stepped forward as a state-space system at each stage, or \(f_{hs}\) and \(f_{pto}\), which are evaluated from the current state.

docs.title: Interpolation schemes
docs.text:
The interpolation dict in the solver config is passed directly to scipy.interpolate.interp1d via the kind keyword:

kind Description Accuracy "linear" (default) Piecewise linear between grid points 2nd order in grid spacing "nearest" Zero-order hold — value at nearest grid point 1st order (step function) "quadratic" Piecewise quadratic spline 3rd order "cubic" Piecewise cubic spline 4th order

docs.title: Consistency with the ODE solver
docs.text:
A subtle point: if you use RK4 ("method": "RK4") but hold the forcing constant within a step ("kind": "nearest"), the integration is effectively first-order in the forcing term. The radiation and restoring forces benefit from the full RK4 accuracy, but the excitation forcing does not. For best results, match the interpolation order to the solver:

  • RK4 / RK2: use "linear" or "cubic"
  • Euler: "nearest" (ZOH) is sufficient and cheapest

In practice, "linear" is a good default — it is cheap and ensures that \(f_e^{lin}\) varies smoothly across RK stages.

docs.title: Practical note on grid resolution
docs.text: The interpolation error decreases as the handled data timestep decreases. If you notice artefacts in simulated time series (especially at high frequencies), try reducing dt in the handle config to produce a finer forcing grid, rather than switching to a higher-order interpolation scheme.
